response: Yes, different follow-up modalities could play a role in the diagnosis of asymptomatic endometrial cancer relapses. According to the available data, women with asymptomatic recurrence have shown a better clinical outcome compared with those with symptomatic relapse. However, the optimal approach is currently unknown, and guidelines comparing follow-up protocols have not been established. Prospective cost-effectiveness studies are needed to determine the most effective follow-up modality for diagnosing asymptomatic endometrial cancer relapses. Additionally, imaging modalities such as diffusion-weighted MR imaging may be helpful in the detection of uterine endometrial cancer in nonenhanced MR imaging, which could potentially aid in the diagnosis of asymptomatic relapses.
